reconstructed_theorem_text:
Objects: Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. q is the supplied elementary-process record with deterministic strictly increasing times t_0,...,t_n and real coefficient functions q_i. Its value is q.value(t,omega)=sum_{i=0}^{n-1} 1_{t_i<t<=t_{i+1}}*q_i(omega), zero outside the union of these left-open, right-closed intervals.

Domains: Omega with measurable space m; filtration on R_+; n in N; q:ElementaryAdaptedProcess(filtration,n); T>=0; omega in Omega. No measure on Omega is present.

Quantifiers: Universally Omega,m,filtration,n,q,T,omega. The q record itself includes for every cell i a strongly-measurable coefficient and an existential bound C_i valid for every omega.

Assumptions: The times t_i in R_+ are strictly increasing. Each q_i:Omega->R is strongly measurable with respect to filtration(t_i), and for each i there exists C_i with |q_i(omega)|<=C_i for every omega. There is no stated t_0=0, t_n=T, or T>0 requirement.

Conclusion: For every T and omega, integral_0^T q.value(t,omega)^2 dt = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} q_i(omega)^2 * real(min(t_{i+1},T)-min(t_i,T)), where subtraction on the right is performed in R_+ before casting.

Scopes: An exact deterministic identity for every sample point, not an almost-everywhere equality. The interval lengths are clipped by T. The value function uses intervals (t_i,t_{i+1}], and vanishes at t_0 and outside their union.

Constant dependencies: The per-cell bound C_i may depend on q and i, but is independent of omega. These bounds do not appear in the identity. No global measure or expectation is involved.
